author: mac_eth
text:
UPDATE ON SURPLUS:

First, if you're new here, we're building https://t.co/6D1YcYIiD4.

We're an inference provider based on an open market. For high volume buyers, the market prices have been better than the prices you can get anywhere else.

Our median discounts have been 40-60% vs other major inference providers. At a 50% discount, it means 2x as much inference for the same amount of spend.

If you're building an AI product, you should definitely check us out!

----

I'm also building in the open. And this inspired someone to create a coin, $surplus.

The creator is unknown but they gave the trading fees to my twitter account. I used some of the fees to get a few months of runway for a team.

----

Some major work completed by the team last month:

1. Migration to AWS (was completed faster than expected, props to the team).

2. Stripe payment support. Soon after adding this, we saw both; (1) some incremental payment volume, and (2) a shift from crypto to Stripe even though most current users are crypto natives and even though Stripe's fees are high -- both validate the decision to prioritize fiat support.

3. UI revamp. Site looks totally different now; no longer the basic template I made with Claude lol.

----

A few next priorities:

1. Major rework of the orderbook / routing / offer health logic. This is a large chunk of work but will address a lot of feedback we've gotten from both buyers and sellers.

2. Adding support for multi-tenant accounts and more features for business users. This prepares us to onboard business users.

3. Improvements to our media model offerings (image, video, ...).

4. Growth: cold outreach, seo, tech influencer marketing, ... .

----

Revenue:

We still have 0% fees. We have roughly $1000-2000 of daily payment volume now, so if we turned on fees up to 5% we'd expect up to $50-100/day in revenue.

We've made 69.82 ETH from all time trading fees, all of which is being swapped to USDC that is used for paying the team and other business costs (AWS credits, ...).

We're continuing to explore options for increasing runway. We are taking our time on this to be sure we land on something fair to the token community and durable for us as a business that wants to grow rapidly.

We aren't planning to sell $Surplus for more runway.

----

We also love feedback from our users, and we shape our priorities around what we hear from you.

Let us know what features you'd like to see on Surplus!

What are we missing?
What is working well?
What is confusing or frustrating?
...

The best part of building in the open is hearing from you!

author: randylunetto
text:
since we decided to NOT pay for an expensive marketing email platform (like drip) to create and send from, ive been kinda stuck sending our weekly newsletter as a plain text email from the marketing email studio platform i built with claude code. theres just no way im going to be able to vibe code a high quality email design editor as good as drip for example..already been down that road and burned way too many tokens $$ its not worth it. but now we've established a marketing partnership with a serious local company, and if we're going to mention their name in our newsletter then its time to upgrade the look/feel of our newsletter to be more pretty and professional for our audiences.

i saw a post yesterday that @AnthropicAI just released artifacts on claude code via @ClaudeDevs, which   reminded how well claude builds html artifacts.. which is perfect for email design! so i implemented a new workflow around that... all i had to do was build a "Compose with HTML" feature in my email studio platform (one shotted it in 5 mins) so my partner who owns the weekly newsletter can just compose and design the email in claude as an html artifact and copy/paste or import the html into our email studio platform.

quotedTweet.text:
its so insane to think about how we paid drip thousands of dollars a month at our last start up to power email stuff

i built my own email marketing studio paltform tailored to what i need and costs $15 a month with @postmarkapp lol

how we got here:
>started with manual emails via gmail and pulling user emails from db manually with a 'reply stop' line ;) 
>manually pulled email lists every week and manually removed users from email list who replied stop 
>no email tracking but obvious evidence that newsletters boosted user engagement - enough signal to keep sending newsletters
>user email count got too big, started getting blocked by gmail
>built a a newsletter composer app with lovable, connected to my prod db and powered by postmark
>now newsletters are fully automated except writing the content. oh and we got tracking in postmark too (nice!) but had to log into to postmark to see stuff
>social media marketing is time expensive, what else can we do to boost engagement and sales? newsletters work decent, so lets try targeted email campaigns!
>extended my simple newsletter composer app with @Lovable into a full fledged email marketing platform
>i used lovable and @claudeai  code and @supabase edge functions to set up all of my triggers and the guard rails and run simulations with testing features using live prod db data to understand what would happen if we went live and iterated from there
>went live yesterday and its running perfectly! we currently have 3 targeted email campaigns running autonomously and dashboard pulls in the postmark analytics into our dashboard for easy viewing
>going to add a few more this week and see what happens

the jump from simple newsletter composter to full automated targeted email platform with triggers/guardrails/analytics etc took me a couple full days of work and not spending hundreds on some bloated crm/marketing tool like drip (sorry drip loved you but now useless)
